why: Divisibility of a sum depends only on remainders: (a + b) % x == 0 exactly when a % x and b % x add up to 0 or x. Bucket prices by remainder and pair bucket r with bucket x - r, counting r = 0 (and r = x/2) within one bucket.
hints: Checking every pair is O(n^2). What property of a price decides whether it can pair with another?
Only p % x matters: remainders r and (x - r) % x pair up. Count how many prices fall in each remainder.
For each remainder r with complement c = (x - r) % x: if r == c add cnt*(cnt-1)/2, else if r < c add cnt[r]*cnt[c]. O(n) with a hash map (x can be 2*10^9, so not an array).
pitfalls: Remainder 0 pairs with itself, and so does x/2 when x is even: count C(k, 2) there.
Count each pair of buckets once (only when r < complement).
x is up to 2*10^9: use a hash map of remainders, not an array of size x.
